outputs: Universal adversarial triggers for text classification

normalized.natural adversarial triggers for text cl: Universal adversarial triggers for text classification

changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate SNLI dataset entry, normalized ARAE to full form, consolidated and normalized output descriptions, added IMDB dataset mentioned in transferability experiments
Consolidated duplicate entries and normalized to base forms: grouped all grammar checker metrics under 'Grammar Checker Errors' and all GPT-2 based metrics under 'GPT-2 Loss'
No LLMs were used as judges - GPT-2 was only used as a language model for automatic evaluation, not for judging outputs post-generation

guideline: Workers compare pairs of triggers to select the more natural one
Workers judge whether individual text samples are naturally generated or not

changes_made.explanation: Added 'fluency' as an explicit criterion mentioned in the paper, removed 'detectability' which was not explicitly mentioned as a human evaluation criterion

overall_notes: The paper focuses on generating natural adversarial triggers for text classification systems. While it involves text generation (adversarial triggers), the primary focus is on attacking classifiers rather than evaluating NLG quality per se. The human evaluations specifically assess the naturalness and fluency of the generated triggers compared to baseline methods.
